points.meaning: as for; marks the topic of the sentence
points.formation: Noun + は
points.ex_ja: 私は学生です。
points.ex_en: I am a student.
points.notes: Written は but pronounced 'wa'. It sets up what the sentence is about; the key information comes after it.

points.meaning: marks the subject; points out new or focused information
points.formation: Noun + が
points.ex_ja: 雨が降っています。
points.ex_en: It is raining.
points.notes: Question words such as だれ and 何 take が, never は, when they are the subject. が is also used with 好き, ほしい, 上手 and わかる for the thing liked, wanted or understood.

points.meaning: marks the direct object of a verb; marks a place moved through or left
points.formation: Noun + を
points.ex_ja: 毎朝パンを食べます。
points.ex_en: I eat bread every morning.
points.notes: Written を but pronounced 'o'. With movement verbs such as 歩く, 散歩する and 出る it marks the route or the place being left.

points.meaning: at; on; in (a specific point in time)
points.formation: Noun + に
points.ex_ja: 毎朝7時に起きます。
points.ex_en: I get up at seven every morning.
points.notes: Used with clock times, dates, days of the week and months. Relative words such as 今日, 明日, 毎日 and 来週 take no に.

points.meaning: to; into (the destination of movement)
points.formation: Noun + に + 行く / 来る / 帰る
points.ex_ja: 毎日バスで学校に行きます。
points.ex_en: I go to school by bus every day.
points.notes: Close in meaning to へ. に puts the focus on the arrival point, へ on the direction.

points.meaning: in; at; on (where someone or something is)
points.formation: Noun + に + ある / いる
points.ex_ja: 机の上に辞書があります。
points.ex_en: There is a dictionary on the desk.
points.notes: Used with ある, いる and 住む. For the place where an action happens (eat, study, play), use で instead.

points.meaning: to (the person who receives or is the target of an action)
points.formation: Noun + に
points.ex_ja: 母に手紙を書きます。
points.ex_en: I'm going to write a letter to my mother.
points.notes: Common with あげる, 貸す, 教える, 見せる, 電話をかける and 会う. With もらう and 借りる, に marks the person you get something from.

points.meaning: per; in (how many times within a period)
points.formation: Noun + に + Noun
points.ex_ja: 一週間に二回、プールで泳ぎます。
points.ex_en: I swim in the pool twice a week.
points.notes: The period comes first, then に, then the number of times: 月に一回 (once a month).

points.meaning: to; toward (the direction of movement)
points.formation: Noun + へ
points.ex_ja: 夏休みに北海道へ行きます。
points.ex_en: I'm going to Hokkaido during summer vacation.
points.notes: Written へ but pronounced 'e'. Usually interchangeable with に for destinations; へ stresses the direction a little more.

points.meaning: at; in (the place where an action happens)
points.formation: Noun + で
points.ex_ja: 図書館で本を読みます。
points.ex_en: I read books at the library.
points.notes: Compare 教室にいます (being somewhere: に) with 教室で勉強します (doing something there: で).

points.meaning: by; with; in (means, tool, method or language)
points.formation: Noun + で
points.ex_ja: 毎日電車で会社へ行きます。
points.ex_en: I go to work by train every day.
points.notes: To say 'on foot', use 歩いて行きます rather than で.

points.meaning: and (joining nouns in a complete list)
points.formation: Noun + と + Noun
points.ex_ja: かばんの中にペンとノートがあります。
points.ex_en: There is a pen and a notebook in my bag.
points.notes: と lists every item; to give just some examples, use や. It joins nouns only, not verbs or adjectives.

points.meaning: with; together with (a partner in an action)
points.formation: Noun + と
points.ex_ja: 週末、友達と映画を見ました。
points.ex_en: I saw a movie with a friend on the weekend.
points.notes: Often followed by いっしょに. With verbs like 話す, 会う and 結婚する, と marks the other person.

points.meaning: and (giving some examples out of more); ... and so on
points.formation: Noun + や + Noun
points.ex_ja: 机の上に本や雑誌があります。
points.ex_en: On the desk there are books, magazines and so on.
points.notes: Suggests the list is not complete. Often ends with など: 本や雑誌など.

points.meaning: or (a choice between nouns)
points.formation: Noun + か + Noun
points.ex_ja: 飲み物はコーヒーか紅茶がいいです。
points.ex_en: For a drink, coffee or tea would be good.
points.notes: Means one of the items is chosen. To list items together, use と or や.

points.meaning: also; too; (with a negative) not ... either; neither ... nor
points.formation: Noun + も
points.ex_ja: 私も学生です。
points.ex_en: I'm a student too.
points.notes: も replaces は, が and を, but comes after other particles: 京都にも行きました.

points.meaning: 's; of (possession, belonging or description)
points.formation: Noun + の + Noun
points.ex_ja: これは私のかさです。
points.ex_en: This is my umbrella.
points.notes: The first noun describes the second: 日本の車 (a Japanese car). The second noun can be dropped when clear: それは私のです.

points.meaning: from (a starting point in time or place)
points.formation: Noun + から
points.ex_ja: 授業は9時からです。
points.ex_en: Class starts at nine.
points.notes: Often paired with まで: 月曜日から金曜日まで (from Monday to Friday).

points.meaning: until; up to; as far as
points.formation: Noun + まで
points.ex_ja: 昼休みは1時までです。
points.ex_en: Lunch break is until one o'clock.
points.notes: Marks the end point of something that continues. For a deadline ('by'), use までに (N4).

points.meaning: (question marker) turns a sentence into a question
points.formation: Sentence + か
points.ex_ja: これはあなたのかばんですか。
points.ex_en: Is this your bag?
points.notes: Polite questions end in か and are usually written with 。. In casual speech か is normally dropped and rising intonation is used instead.

points.meaning: isn't it?; right? (seeking agreement or sharing a feeling)
points.formation: Sentence + ね
points.ex_ja: 今日は暑いですね。
points.ex_en: It's hot today, isn't it?
points.notes: Used when the speaker expects the listener to share the same view or knowledge. Compare よ, which tells the listener something new.

points.meaning: you know; I tell you (giving new information or emphasis)
points.formation: Sentence + よ
points.ex_ja: このラーメンはとてもおいしいですよ。
points.ex_en: This ramen is really good, you know.
points.notes: Tells the listener something they may not know. Overusing it with superiors can sound pushy.

points.meaning: than (the standard of comparison)
points.formation: Noun + より
points.ex_ja: 今日はきのうより寒いです。
points.ex_en: Today is colder than yesterday.
points.notes: In X は Y より + adjective, Y is the standard. Japanese adjectives have no '-er' form; より does that job.

points.meaning: X is more ... than Y
points.formation: Noun + の方が + Noun + より
points.ex_ja: 犬の方が猫より好きです。
points.ex_en: I like dogs more than cats.
points.notes: The two parts can come in either order. Often used to answer a どちら question.

points.meaning: which is more ..., X or Y?
points.formation: Noun + と + Noun + とどちらが
points.ex_ja: コーヒーと紅茶とどちらが好きですか。
points.ex_en: Which do you like better, coffee or tea?
points.notes: Compares exactly two things. どっち is the casual form of どちら. Answer with 〜の方が.

points.meaning: ... is the most ... among/of
points.formation: Noun + の中で + Noun + が一番
points.ex_ja: 果物の中でりんごが一番好きです。
points.ex_en: Of all fruits, I like apples the most.
points.notes: Used for three or more items. In questions use 何, だれ, どこ or いつ before が一番.

points.meaning: is; am; are (polite copula)
points.formation: Noun + です / na-Adj + です / i-Adj + です
points.ex_ja: 私はマリアです。
points.ex_en: I'm Maria.
points.notes: Forms: です, ではありません, でした, ではありませんでした. After an い-adjective, です only adds politeness: 高いです.

points.meaning: is; am; are (plain copula)
points.formation: Noun + だ / na-Adj + だ
points.ex_ja: 今日は日曜日だ。
points.ex_en: Today is Sunday.
points.notes: Forms: だ, じゃない, だった, じゃなかった. Never used right after an い-adjective (高いだ is wrong). Often dropped in casual questions: 学生？

points.meaning: is not; am not; are not
points.formation: Noun + ではありません / na-Adj + ではありません / Noun + じゃない / na-Adj + じゃない
points.ex_ja: 私は先生ではありません。学生です。
points.ex_en: I'm not a teacher. I'm a student.
points.notes: じゃありません and じゃないです are more conversational polite forms. Past: ではありませんでした / じゃなかった. い-adjectives use 〜くない instead.

points.meaning: was; were (polite past copula)
points.formation: Noun + でした / na-Adj + でした
points.ex_ja: きのうは私の誕生日でした。
points.ex_en: Yesterday was my birthday.
points.notes: Past negative: ではありませんでした. い-adjectives do not take でした: say 高かったです, not 高いでした.

points.meaning: polite non-past verb ending (do; will do)
points.formation: Verb-stem + ます
points.ex_ja: 毎朝コーヒーを飲みます。
points.ex_en: I drink coffee every morning.
points.notes: Covers habits and future actions. 飲む→飲みます, 食べる→食べます, する→します, 来る→来ます.

points.meaning: do not; will not (polite negative)
points.formation: Verb-stem + ません
points.ex_ja: 私はお酒を飲みません。
points.ex_en: I don't drink alcohol.
points.notes: The plain equivalent is the ない-form: 飲みません = 飲まない.

points.meaning: did (polite past)
points.formation: Verb-stem + ました
points.ex_ja: きのう、友達に会いました。
points.ex_en: I met a friend yesterday.
points.notes: The plain equivalent is the た-form: 会いました = 会った.

points.meaning: did not (polite past negative)
points.formation: Verb-stem + ませんでした
points.ex_ja: けさは朝ご飯を食べませんでした。
points.ex_en: I didn't eat breakfast this morning.
points.notes: The plain equivalent is 〜なかった: 食べませんでした = 食べなかった.

points.meaning: do not; will not (plain negative of verbs)
points.formation: Verb-nai stem + ない
points.ex_ja: 今日は学校へ行かない。
points.ex_en: I'm not going to school today.
points.notes: う-verbs change the last -u sound to -a: 書く→書かない, 買う→買わない. る-verbs drop る: 食べない. する→しない, 来る→こない, ある→ない. Past: 〜なかった.

points.meaning: did (plain past of verbs)
points.formation: Verb-ta
points.ex_ja: 週末は家で映画を見た。
points.ex_en: I watched a movie at home over the weekend.
points.notes: Made exactly like the て-form, with て→た and で→だ: 書いて→書いた, 飲んで→飲んだ, 行って→行った. Polite equivalent: 〜ました.

points.meaning: let's (do)
points.formation: Verb-stem + ましょう
points.ex_ja: いっしょに行きましょう。
points.ex_en: Let's go together.
points.notes: Used when the speaker expects the listener to agree. To invite more gently, use 〜ませんか.

points.meaning: shall I ...?; shall we ...?
points.formation: Verb-stem + ましょうか
points.ex_ja: 窓を開けましょうか。
points.ex_en: Shall I open the window?
points.notes: Offers to do something for the listener (shall I?) or asks them to decide something together (shall we?).

points.meaning: won't you ...?; would you like to ...? (polite invitation)
points.formation: Verb-stem + ませんか
points.ex_ja: いっしょに昼ご飯を食べませんか。
points.ex_en: Would you like to have lunch together?
points.notes: Gentler than 〜ましょう because it leaves the listener room to decline. Accept with ええ、〜ましょう.

points.meaning: want to (do)
points.formation: Verb-stem + たい
points.ex_ja: 夏休みに沖縄へ行きたいです。
points.ex_en: I want to go to Okinawa during summer vacation.
points.notes: Conjugates like an い-adjective: 〜たくない, 〜たかった. The object can take が or を. Not used to state another person's wishes directly.

points.meaning: want (something)
points.formation: Noun + がほしい
points.ex_ja: 新しいパソコンがほしいです。
points.ex_en: I want a new computer.
points.notes: For things, not actions (actions use 〜たい). Conjugates like an い-adjective: ほしくない, ほしかった.

points.meaning: please give me (something); I'll have
points.formation: Noun + をください
points.ex_ja: すみません、水をください。
points.ex_en: Excuse me, could I have some water?
points.notes: Used when shopping or ordering. A quantity goes after を with no particle: 切手を二枚ください.

points.meaning: please (do)
points.formation: Verb-te + ください
points.ex_ja: もう少しゆっくり話してください。
points.ex_en: Please speak a little more slowly.
points.notes: Polite, but still an instruction the speaker expects to be followed. Softer requests use 〜てくれませんか (N4).

points.meaning: please don't (do)
points.formation: Verb-nai + でください
points.ex_ja: 教室で食べないでください。
points.ex_en: Please don't eat in the classroom.
points.notes: Softer than 〜てはいけません. In casual speech ください is dropped: 見ないで.

points.meaning: may; it's okay to
points.formation: Verb-te + もいい
points.ex_ja: この辞書を使ってもいいですか。
points.ex_en: May I use this dictionary?
points.notes: Add ですか to ask for permission. A polite refusal is often just すみません、ちょっと….

points.meaning: must not; may not
points.formation: Verb-te + はいけない
points.ex_ja: 図書館で大きい声で話してはいけません。
points.ex_en: You must not talk loudly in the library.
points.notes: A strong prohibition, often for rules. Polite form: 〜てはいけません. Casual contraction: 〜ちゃいけない / 〜じゃいけない.

points.pattern: 〜なければならない / 〜なくてはいけない
points.meaning: must; have to
points.formation: Verb-nai stem + なければならない / Verb-nai stem + なくてはいけない
points.ex_ja: 明日は6時に起きなければなりません。
points.ex_en: I have to get up at six tomorrow.
points.notes: Polite forms end in なりません / いけません. The two mean the same; なければならない sounds slightly more formal.

points.meaning: don't have to; need not
points.formation: Verb-nai stem + なくてもいい
points.ex_ja: 明日は学校へ来なくてもいいです。
points.ex_en: You don't have to come to school tomorrow.
points.notes: The opposite of 〜なければならない. Ask with 〜なくてもいいですか (Is it all right if I don't ...?).

points.meaning: be doing (ongoing action); be in a state (result of a change); do regularly
points.formation: Verb-te + いる
points.ex_ja: 弟は今、部屋でゲームをしています。
points.ex_en: My younger brother is playing a game in his room now.
points.notes: With action verbs (食べる, 読む) it shows an action in progress; with change verbs (結婚する, 開く, 知る) it shows the resulting state. Polite: 〜ています.

points.meaning: and; and then (linking actions in order)
points.formation: Verb-te + Sentence
points.ex_ja: 朝起きて、顔を洗います。
points.ex_en: I get up in the morning and wash my face.
points.notes: The final verb sets the tense for the whole sentence. 書く→書いて, 飲む→飲んで, 話す→話して, 買う→買って, 行く→行って (irregular).

points.meaning: after doing; (do A) and then (B); since
points.formation: Verb-te + から
points.ex_ja: 手を洗ってから、ご飯を食べましょう。
points.ex_en: Let's wash our hands and then eat.
points.notes: Stresses that A is finished before B starts, more clearly than a plain て. With ている in the main clause it often means 'since'.

points.meaning: do things like A and B; sometimes A, sometimes B
points.formation: Verb-ta + り + Verb-ta + りする
points.ex_ja: 日曜日はそうじをしたり、洗濯をしたりします。
points.ex_en: On Sundays I do things like cleaning and laundry.
points.notes: Picks out a few actions from many. Tense and politeness go on the final する: 〜たりしました.

points.meaning: have (ever) done; have the experience of doing
points.formation: Verb-ta + ことがある
points.ex_ja: 富士山に登ったことがあります。
points.ex_en: I have climbed Mt. Fuji.
points.notes: Talks about life experience, not something just done: きのう食べたことがある is wrong. Negative 〜たことがありません means 'have never'.

points.meaning: before (doing); before (an event); ago
points.formation: Verb-dict + 前に / Noun + の + 前に
points.ex_ja: 寝る前に歯をみがきます。
points.ex_en: I brush my teeth before going to bed.
points.notes: The verb before 前に is always in dictionary form, even when talking about the past. With a length of time there is no の: 3年前に (three years ago).

points.meaning: after (doing); after (an event)
points.formation: Verb-ta + 後で / Noun + の + 後で
points.ex_ja: 晩ご飯を食べた後で、散歩をします。
points.ex_en: I take a walk after eating dinner.
points.notes: The verb before 後で is always in た-form, even for future plans. On its own, 後で means 'later'.

points.meaning: while (doing two actions at the same time)
points.formation: Verb-stem + ながら
points.ex_ja: 音楽を聞きながら勉強します。
points.ex_en: I study while listening to music.
points.notes: Both actions are done by the same person. The main action comes last: in A-ながら B, B is the main activity.

points.meaning: go (somewhere) to do
points.formation: Verb-stem + に行く / Noun + に行く
points.ex_ja: デパートへ服を買いに行きます。
points.ex_en: I'm going to the department store to buy clothes.
points.notes: 来る and 帰る work the same way: 遊びに来る. With する-nouns the noun can come directly: 買い物に行く, 散歩に行く.

points.meaning: like; dislike
points.formation: Noun + が好き / Noun + が嫌い / Verb-dict + の + が好き
points.ex_ja: 私は甘いものが好きです。
points.ex_en: I like sweet things.
points.notes: 好き and 嫌い are な-adjectives, so the thing liked takes が, not を. 大好き and 大嫌い are stronger. 嫌い can sound blunt; あまり好きじゃない is softer.

points.meaning: good at; bad at
points.formation: Noun + が上手 / Noun + が下手
points.ex_ja: 姉はピアノが上手です。
points.ex_en: My older sister is good at the piano.
points.notes: Mostly used about other people; calling yourself 上手 can sound like bragging. Both are な-adjectives: 料理が上手な人.

points.meaning: there is; there are; have (ある for things, いる for people and animals)
points.formation: Noun + がある / Noun + がいる
points.ex_ja: 公園に大きい木があります。
points.ex_en: There is a big tree in the park.
points.notes: ある is for things, plants and events; いる is for people and animals. Negatives: ない / いない (polite: ありません / いません).

points.meaning: because; since; so
points.formation: Sentence + から
points.ex_ja: 今日は寒いから、コートを着ます。
points.ex_en: It's cold today, so I'll wear a coat.
points.notes: The reason comes first: A から B (A, so B). Answer どうして with 〜からです. Nouns and な-adjectives need だ: 雨だから.

points.meaning: but; although
points.formation: Sentence + が
points.ex_ja: この店は安いですが、あまりおいしくないです。
points.ex_en: This restaurant is cheap, but the food isn't very good.
points.notes: Also used just to soften a request or lead into a topic: すみませんが…. A little more formal than けど (N4).

points.meaning: probably; I think; ..., right?
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + でしょう
points.ex_ja: 明日は雨が降るでしょう。
points.ex_en: It will probably rain tomorrow.
points.notes: Typical of weather forecasts. Said with rising intonation, it asks the listener to agree. Plain form: だろう (N4).

points.meaning: become; get; turn
points.formation: i-Adj-ku + なる / na-Adj + になる / Noun + になる
points.ex_ja: あたたかくなりましたね。
points.ex_en: It's gotten warmer, hasn't it?
points.notes: いい becomes よくなる. Often used in the past to describe a change that has happened: 大きくなりました.

points.meaning: decide on; choose; I'll have
points.formation: Noun + にする
points.ex_ja: 私はカレーにします。
points.ex_en: I'll have the curry.
points.notes: Common when ordering food or picking from options. Past: 〜にしました (I decided on ...).

points.meaning: not yet (have done)
points.formation: まだ + Verb-te + いない / まだ + Verb-te + いません
points.ex_ja: まだ昼ご飯を食べていません。
points.ex_en: I haven't eaten lunch yet.
points.notes: Use ていない, not ませんでした, for something that may still happen. The short answer is いいえ、まだです.

points.meaning: already (have done); (in questions) yet
points.formation: もう + Verb-ta / もう + Verb-stem + ました
points.ex_ja: 「もう晩ご飯を食べましたか。」「はい、もう食べました。」
points.ex_en: "Have you eaten dinner yet?" "Yes, I already have."
points.notes: In questions もう means 'yet'. With a negative verb, もう means 'no longer': もう食べません.

points.meaning: not very; not much; not often
points.formation: あまり + Verb-nai / あまり + i-Adj-ku + ない / あまり + na-Adj + じゃない
points.ex_ja: 私はあまりテレビを見ません。
points.ex_en: I don't watch much TV.
points.notes: Always followed by a negative form. あまり好きじゃない is a softer way to say you dislike something.

points.meaning: not at all; not in the least
points.formation: 全然 + Verb-nai / 全然 + i-Adj-ku + ない / 全然 + na-Adj + じゃない
points.ex_ja: この問題は全然わかりません。
points.ex_en: I don't understand this question at all.
points.notes: Stronger than あまり〜ない. In casual speech 全然 is sometimes used with positive words (全然大丈夫), but with a negative is the standard use.

points.meaning: only; just
points.formation: Noun + だけ / Verb-dict + だけ
points.ex_ja: 財布に100円だけあります。
points.ex_en: I only have 100 yen in my wallet.
points.notes: Neutral in tone. Compare しか〜ない (N4), which stresses that the amount is small.

points.meaning: about; approximately (an amount or length of time)
points.formation: Noun + くらい / Noun + ぐらい
points.ex_ja: 駅まで歩いて10分ぐらいです。
points.ex_en: It's about a ten-minute walk to the station.
points.notes: Used with amounts and durations. For a point in time (around three o'clock), use ごろ: 3時ごろ.

points.meaning: around; about (a point in time)
points.formation: Noun + ごろ
points.ex_ja: 毎晩11時ごろ寝ます。
points.ex_en: I go to bed around eleven every night.
points.notes: Attaches to clock times, dates and months. に after ごろ is optional: 7時ごろ(に)起きます.

points.pattern: 何も〜ない / 誰も〜ない
points.romaji: nani mo ... nai / dare mo ... nai
points.meaning: nothing; nobody; not anything; not anyone
points.formation: 何も + Verb-nai / 誰も + Verb-nai
points.ex_ja: けさは何も食べませんでした。
points.ex_en: I didn't eat anything this morning.
points.notes: With places, a particle comes before も: どこにも / どこへも行きません (go nowhere). 誰 is often written in hiragana: だれ.

points.pattern: 何か / 誰か / どこか
points.romaji: nani ka / dare ka / doko ka
points.meaning: something; someone; somewhere
points.formation: Question word + か
points.ex_ja: 何か飲みますか。
points.ex_en: Would you like something to drink?
points.notes: Question word + か gives 'some-' words; question word + も + negative gives 'no-' words. が and を after 何か / だれか are often dropped.

points.pattern: これ / それ / あれ / どれ
points.meaning: this one; that one (near you); that one (over there); which one
points.formation: これ / それ / あれ / どれ
points.ex_ja: これは私の辞書です。
points.ex_en: This is my dictionary.
points.notes: こ = near the speaker, そ = near the listener, あ = away from both, ど = question. They stand alone; as a subject どれ takes が, not は.

points.pattern: この / その / あの / どの
points.meaning: this; that (near you); that ... over there; which (before a noun)
points.formation: この / その / あの / どの + Noun
points.ex_ja: このケーキはおいしいです。
points.ex_en: This cake is delicious.
points.notes: Always followed by a noun: この本, never この alone. これ / それ / あれ / どれ are used when there is no noun.

points.pattern: ここ / そこ / あそこ / どこ
points.meaning: here; there (near you); over there; where
points.formation: ここ / そこ / あそこ / どこ
points.ex_ja: ここは私の学校です。
points.ex_en: This is my school.
points.notes: こちら / そちら / あちら / どちら are politer versions: お国はどちらですか (Where are you from?).

points.meaning: negative and past forms of i-adjectives (is not; was; was not)
points.formation: i-Adj stem + くない / i-Adj stem + かった / i-Adj stem + くなかった
points.ex_ja: この部屋はあまり広くないです。
points.ex_en: This room isn't very big.
points.notes: 高い→高くない, 高かった, 高くなかった. Add です to be polite. いい is irregular: よくない, よかった, よくなかった.

points.meaning: na-adjectives: take な before a noun and です or だ at the end of a sentence
points.formation: na-Adj + な + Noun / na-Adj + です / na-Adj + ではありません / na-Adj + でした
points.ex_ja: 京都は有名な町です。
points.ex_en: Kyoto is a famous city.
points.notes: Before a noun, add な: 静かな部屋. At the end of a sentence they change like nouns. きれい and きらい end in い but are な-adjectives.

points.meaning: and (linking adjectives or nouns)
points.formation: i-Adj-ku + て / na-Adj + で / Noun + で
points.ex_ja: この店は安くておいしいです。
points.ex_en: This restaurant is cheap and good.
points.notes: いい becomes よくて. Join qualities that point the same way (both good or both bad); for a contrast, use が instead.

points.meaning: called; named
points.formation: Noun + という + Noun
points.ex_ja: これは「すきやき」という料理です。
points.ex_en: This is a dish called sukiyaki.
points.notes: Introduces a name the listener may not know.

points.pattern: あげる / くれる / もらう
points.meaning: give (to someone else); give (to me or my group); receive
points.formation: Noun (receiver) + に + Noun + を + あげる / Noun (giver) + が + Noun + を + くれる / Noun (giver) + に + Noun + を + もらう
points.ex_ja: 私は弟に古いゲームをあげた。
points.ex_en: I gave my old game to my little brother.
points.notes: くれる is used only when the receiver is the speaker or someone in the speaker's group. With もらう the giver can be marked with に or から.

points.meaning: do something for someone (as a favor)
points.formation: Verb-te + あげる
points.ex_ja: 妹の宿題を手伝ってあげました。
points.ex_en: I helped my little sister with her homework.
points.notes: Said directly to a superior it can sound condescending; use the humble お〜しましょうか (お持ちしましょうか) instead.

points.meaning: someone does something for me (or my group)
points.formation: Verb-te + くれる
points.ex_ja: 友達が引っ越しを手伝ってくれた。
points.ex_en: A friend helped me move.
points.notes: The subject is the person doing the favor; the one who benefits is the speaker or someone close to them.

points.meaning: have someone do something (for me); get someone to do
points.formation: Verb-te + もらう
points.ex_ja: 先輩にレポートを見てもらった。
points.ex_en: I had a senior student look over my report.
points.notes: The receiver of the favor is the subject, and the person who does the action is marked with に.

points.meaning: (honorific) someone kindly does for me; (humble) I receive the favor of someone doing
points.formation: Verb-te + くださる / Verb-te + いただく
points.ex_ja: 先生が私の作文を直してくださいました。
points.ex_en: My teacher kindly corrected my essay.
points.notes: くださる is the honorific version of くれる (ます-form: くださいます); いただく is the humble version of もらう.

points.meaning: do something and go; go on doing (from now into the future)
points.formation: Verb-te + いく
points.ex_ja: 雨が降りそうだから、傘を持っていきます。
points.ex_en: It looks like rain, so I'll take an umbrella.
points.notes: Movement or change away from the speaker, or from now toward the future. Compare 〜てくる.

points.meaning: do something and come back; come doing; (change) up to now; start to
points.formation: Verb-te + くる
points.ex_ja: ちょっとコンビニに行ってきます。
points.ex_en: I'm just popping out to the convenience store.
points.notes: Movement or change toward the speaker, or from the past up to now. 行ってきます literally means 'I'll go and come back.'

points.meaning: finish completely; do by accident; end up doing (with regret)
points.formation: Verb-te + しまう
points.ex_ja: 電車に傘を忘れてしまいました。
points.ex_en: I left my umbrella on the train.
points.notes: In speech 〜てしまう contracts to 〜ちゃう, and 〜でしまう to 〜じゃう (飲んじゃう).

points.meaning: do in advance (to prepare); do and leave as is
points.formation: Verb-te + おく
points.ex_ja: 旅行の前に、ホテルを予約しておきます。
points.ex_en: I'll book the hotel before the trip.
points.notes: In casual speech 〜ておく often becomes 〜とく (買っとく), and 〜でおく becomes 〜どく (読んどく).

points.meaning: try doing (to see what it is like)
points.formation: Verb-te + みる
points.ex_ja: このシャツ、着てみてもいいですか。
points.ex_en: May I try this shirt on?
points.notes: Means trying something out to see the result, not making an effort to do something difficult.

points.meaning: has been done (and stays that way); resulting state of a deliberate action
points.formation: Verb-te + ある
points.ex_ja: 入り口に地図がはってあります。
points.ex_en: There's a map put up at the entrance.
points.notes: Used with transitive verbs, and the object usually takes が. It implies someone did it on purpose, unlike 〜ている with intransitive verbs (窓が開いている).

points.meaning: when; at the time when
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + とき
points.ex_ja: 子どものとき、よく川で泳ぎました。
points.ex_en: When I was a child, I often swam in the river.
points.notes: The verb's tense shows the order: 行くとき means before or on the way (the going isn't finished yet); 行ったとき means after arriving. Often written 時 in kanji.

points.meaning: while; during (the whole time); at some point during
points.formation: Verb-te + いる / Verb-dict / Noun + の + 間（に）
points.ex_ja: 夏休みの間、祖父の家にいました。
points.ex_en: I stayed at my grandfather's house during the summer vacation.
points.notes: 間 means the action continues through the whole period; 間に means it happens at some point within the period.

points.meaning: looks like; seems; looks about to
points.formation: Verb-stem / i-Adj stem / na-Adj + そうだ
points.ex_ja: そのカレー、辛そうだね。
points.ex_en: That curry looks spicy.
points.notes: A judgment from what you see. いい → よさそう, ない → なさそう. Not used with adjectives for plainly visible traits (赤い, かわいい); かわいそう means 'pitiful'.

points.meaning: I heard that; they say that
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj + そうだ / na-Adj + だ + そうだ / Noun + だ + そうだ
points.ex_ja: 天気予報では、明日は雪が降るそうです。
points.ex_en: The weather forecast says it will snow tomorrow.
points.notes: Attaches to full plain forms, unlike the 'looks like' そうだ, which attaches to stems. It has no past or negative form.

points.meaning: apparently; it seems; I hear
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + らしい
points.ex_ja: 駅の近くに新しいカフェができたらしい。
points.ex_en: Apparently a new café has opened near the station.
points.notes: Based on something heard or read, so the speaker sounds a little detached. The 'typical of' らしい (男らしい) is a separate N3 point.

points.meaning: it seems; it appears (judging from evidence)
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj + ようだ / na-Adj + な + ようだ / Noun + の + ようだ
points.ex_ja: 誰もいないようですね。
points.ex_en: It seems nobody's here.
points.notes: A somewhat formal way to state a judgment from what you observe or feel; みたいだ is the casual equivalent. The 'like, as if' use is covered at N3.

points.meaning: seems like; looks like; like (casual)
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + みたい
points.ex_ja: 隣の部屋に誰か来たみたい。
points.ex_en: Sounds like someone has come to the room next door.
points.notes: Casual equivalent of ようだ. It attaches directly to nouns and na-adjectives (静かみたい) without な or の. Before a noun it becomes みたいな.

points.meaning: too; too much; excessively
points.formation: Verb-stem / i-Adj stem / na-Adj + すぎる
points.ex_ja: ゆうべ飲みすぎて、頭が痛い。
points.ex_en: I drank too much last night, and now I have a headache.
points.notes: Conjugates like a Group 2 verb (すぎた, すぎて). いい → よすぎる, and the adjective ない → なさすぎる.

points.meaning: how to; way of doing
points.formation: Verb-stem + 方
points.ex_ja: この機械の使い方を教えてください。
points.ex_en: Please show me how to use this machine.
points.notes: The result is a noun, so the object takes の instead of を (日本語の話し方). With する-verbs: 勉強のしかた.

points.meaning: in the middle of; during (ちゅう); throughout; all over (じゅう)
points.formation: Noun + 中
points.ex_ja: 父は今、電話中です。
points.ex_en: My father is on the phone right now.
points.notes: ちゅう marks an ongoing activity or a period (会議中, 午前中, 今週中); じゅう means 'throughout' a time or place (一日中, 世界中).

points.meaning: intend to; plan to
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + つもり
points.ex_ja: 夏休みは北海道を旅行するつもりです。
points.ex_en: I intend to travel around Hokkaido during the summer break.
points.notes: States a firm personal intention. 〜つもりはない means 'have no intention of'. Asking a superior 〜つもりですか can sound blunt.

points.meaning: plan to; be scheduled to
points.formation: Verb-dict + 予定 / Noun + の + 予定
points.ex_ja: 来月、大阪に引っ越す予定です。
points.ex_en: I'm planning to move to Osaka next month.
points.notes: Refers to a fixed schedule or arrangement, often involving other people; more objective than つもり.

points.meaning: decide to
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ことにする
points.ex_ja: 健康のために、毎朝歩くことにした。
points.ex_en: I decided to walk every morning for my health.
points.notes: A decision made by the speaker; compare 〜ことになる. 〜ことにしている (N3) means 'make it a rule to'.

points.meaning: it has been decided that; it turns out that
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ことになる
points.ex_ja: 来年の春から、名古屋の店で働くことになりました。
points.ex_en: It's been decided that I'll work at the Nagoya store from next spring.
points.notes: Presents a decision as made by others or by circumstances. People also use it for their own decisions to sound less assertive.

points.meaning: can; be able to; be possible to
points.formation: Verb-dict + ことができる
points.ex_ja: この図書館では、本を二週間借りることができます。
points.ex_en: At this library, you can borrow books for two weeks.
points.notes: A bit more formal than the potential form. Also used for what is possible or allowed (ここでたばこを吸うことはできません).

points.meaning: can; be able to (potential form)
points.formation: Verb-dict (Group 1: final u → e) + る / Verb-nai stem + られる (Group 2)
points.ex_ja: 私は漢字が二百ぐらい読めます。
points.ex_en: I can read about two hundred kanji.
points.notes: Irregular: する → できる, 来る → 来られる. The object often takes が instead of を. In casual speech Group 2 verbs often drop ら (見れる).

points.meaning: be done (by someone); passive voice
points.formation: Verb-nai stem + れる (Group 1) / Verb-nai stem + られる (Group 2)
points.ex_ja: 先生に作文をほめられました。
points.ex_en: My essay was praised by my teacher.
points.notes: Irregular: する → される, 来る → 来られる. The doer is marked with に. Often shows that the subject was troubled by someone's action (雨に降られた).

points.meaning: make someone do; let someone do (causative)
points.formation: Verb-nai stem + せる (Group 1) / Verb-nai stem + させる (Group 2)
points.ex_ja: 母は毎日弟に野菜を食べさせる。
points.ex_en: My mother makes my little brother eat vegetables every day.
points.notes: Irregular: する → させる, 来る → 来させる. With intransitive verbs the person takes を; with transitive verbs, に. Context decides 'make' or 'let'.

points.meaning: be made to do (against one's will)
points.formation: Verb-nai stem + せられる (Group 1; short form される) / Verb-nai stem + させられる (Group 2)
points.ex_ja: 子どものころ、母に毎日ピアノを練習させられた。
points.ex_en: When I was a child, my mother made me practice the piano every day.
points.notes: Irregular: する → させられる, 来る → 来させられる. The short Group 1 form (待たされる) is common in speech, but not with verbs ending in す (話させられる).

points.meaning: let's (casual); I'll (volitional form)
points.formation: Verb-dict (Group 1: final u → o) + う / Verb-stem + よう (Group 2)
points.ex_ja: 疲れたね。少し休もう。
points.ex_en: That was tiring, huh? Let's take a short break.
points.notes: Irregular: する → しよう, 来る → 来よう. The plain equivalent of 〜ましょう.

points.meaning: be thinking of doing; plan to
points.formation: Verb-volitional + と思う
points.ex_ja: 今年の夏は海に行こうと思っています。
points.ex_en: I'm thinking of going to the beach this summer.
points.notes: 〜と思う often reports a decision made just now; 〜と思っている shows a plan held for some time. Softer than つもり.

points.meaning: do it! (imperative form; blunt command)
points.formation: Verb-dict (Group 1: final u → e) / Verb-stem + ろ (Group 2)
points.ex_ja: 早く起きろ！遅刻するぞ。
points.ex_en: Get up already! You'll be late.
points.notes: Irregular: する → しろ, 来る → 来い, くれる → くれ. Very blunt; heard mainly from men, on signs, in emergencies and in cheering (がんばれ).

points.meaning: don't! (strong prohibition)
points.formation: Verb-dict + な
points.ex_ja: 危ないから、この川では泳ぐな。
points.ex_en: It's dangerous, so don't swim in this river.
points.notes: Very strong and blunt. Do not confuse it with the sentence-ending な that expresses feeling (いいな).

points.meaning: do (instruction from a parent, teacher, etc.)
points.formation: Verb-stem + なさい
points.ex_ja: もう九時よ。早く寝なさい。
points.ex_en: It's already nine. Go to bed now.
points.notes: Softer than the imperative form but still a firm instruction; used by parents, teachers and in exam directions, never toward superiors.

points.meaning: if
points.formation: Verb-ba / i-Adj stem + ければ / na-Adj + なら / Noun + なら
points.ex_ja: この道をまっすぐ行けば、駅に着きます。
points.ex_en: If you go straight along this road, you'll reach the station.
points.notes: Focuses on the condition needed for a result. When the main clause is a request or invitation, たら is usually more natural unless the ば-clause is a state (ある, いる, adjectives).

points.meaning: if; when; after
points.formation: Verb-ta + ら / i-Adj stem + かったら / na-Adj + だったら / Noun + だったら
points.ex_ja: 駅に着いたら、電話してください。
points.ex_en: Please call me when you get to the station.
points.notes: The most versatile conditional and very common in speech. With events certain to happen it means 'when/after'.

points.meaning: if (it's the case that); if you're talking about
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + なら
points.ex_ja: 京都へ行くなら、秋がいいですよ。
points.ex_en: If you're going to Kyoto, autumn is a good time.
points.notes: Takes up what the listener said or a situation assumed to be true, then gives advice or an opinion. Unlike たら, the main action can come before the なら-clause.

points.meaning: when; if; whenever (natural or automatic result)
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-nai / i-Adj + と / na-Adj + だ + と / Noun + だ + と
points.ex_ja: このボタンを押すと、お茶が出ます。
points.ex_en: When you press this button, tea comes out.
points.notes: For natural results, how machines work, directions and habits. The main clause cannot be a request, wish or invitation.

points.meaning: even if; even though
points.formation: Verb-te + も / i-Adj-ku + ても / na-Adj + でも / Noun + でも
points.ex_ja: 雨が降っても、試合はあります。
points.ex_en: Even if it rains, the game will go ahead.
points.notes: With question words or いくら it means 'no matter ...' (何を食べても, いくら待っても).

points.meaning: although; even though (with surprise or dissatisfaction)
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj + のに / na-Adj + な + のに / Noun + な + のに
points.ex_ja: 一生懸命勉強したのに、試験に落ちてしまった。
points.ex_en: Even though I studied really hard, I failed the exam.
points.notes: Carries surprise, disappointment or complaint. The main clause cannot be a request or intention; use けど or ても there.

points.meaning: for; in order to (with use, time or cost)
points.formation: Verb-dict + のに / Noun + に
points.ex_ja: このかばんは旅行に行くのに便利です。
points.ex_en: This bag is handy for traveling.
points.notes: Usually followed by words like 使う, いい, 便利, 必要 or かかる. With a noun, just に is used (旅行に便利).

points.meaning: because; since
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj + ので / na-Adj + な + ので / Noun + な + ので
points.ex_ja: 頭が痛いので、今日は早く帰ります。
points.ex_en: I have a headache, so I'm going home early today.
points.notes: Sounds softer and more objective than から, so it is preferred when giving reasons politely or apologizing.

points.meaning: because; so (cause of a feeling or state)
points.formation: Verb-te / i-Adj stem + くて / na-Adj + で / Noun + で
points.ex_ja: ニュースを聞いて、びっくりしました。
points.ex_en: I was surprised to hear the news.
points.notes: The second part is usually a feeling, a potential form or a result, not a request or intention (use から or ので for those). Negative: 〜なくて (会えなくて寂しい).

points.meaning: and what's more; and besides (listing reasons)
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj + し / na-Adj + だ + し / Noun + だ + し
points.ex_ja: この部屋は広いし、駅から近いし、とても気に入っています。
points.ex_en: This apartment is spacious and close to the station, so I really like it.
points.notes: Lists several reasons or points. A single し hints that there are other reasons too.

points.meaning: but; although; (soft lead-in)
points.formation: Sentence + けど / けれども
points.ex_ja: この店は高いけど、おいしい。
points.ex_en: This place is expensive, but the food is good.
points.notes: More conversational than が; けれども is a little more formal than けど. Often used as a soft lead-in before a question or request.

points.meaning: in order to; for (the sake of); because of
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-ta / Noun + の + ために
points.ex_ja: 日本の大学に入るために、毎日勉強しています。
points.ex_en: I study every day in order to get into a Japanese university.
points.notes: For purpose, the verb must be something the subject can control (compare 〜ように). The 'because of' use sounds fairly formal.

points.meaning: so that; in order that
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ように
points.ex_ja: 後ろの人にも聞こえるように、大きな声で話してください。
points.ex_en: Please speak loudly so that the people in the back can hear too.
points.notes: Used with verbs the subject can't directly control: potential forms, 分かる, 見える, negatives. For deliberate actions use ために.

points.meaning: try to; make sure to; make a habit of
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ようにする
points.ex_ja: 毎日野菜を食べるようにしています。
points.ex_en: I make a point of eating vegetables every day.
points.notes: 〜ようにしている describes a habit you keep up. Compare 〜ようになる, a change that comes about.

points.meaning: come to; reach the point where (change in ability or habit)
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ようになる
points.ex_ja: 練習して、自転車に乗れるようになりました。
points.ex_en: After practicing, I became able to ride a bike.
points.notes: Often used with potential verbs. For 'no longer', 〜なくなる is usually more natural than 〜ないようになる.

points.meaning: want someone to do
points.formation: Verb-te + ほしい / Verb-nai + で + ほしい
points.ex_ja: もう少しゆっくり話してほしいです。
points.ex_en: I'd like you to speak a little more slowly.
points.notes: The person you want to act is marked with に. Said to a superior it can sound demanding; 〜ていただきたいです is more polite.

points.meaning: (someone else) wants to
points.formation: Verb-stem + たがる
points.ex_ja: 子どもたちは外で遊びたがっている。
points.ex_en: The children want to play outside.
points.notes: Used for other people, since you can't directly know their wishes. Current wishes are usually expressed with 〜たがっている.

points.meaning: (someone else) feels; shows signs of feeling
points.formation: i-Adj stem / na-Adj + がる
points.ex_ja: 妹は暗い所を怖がる。
points.ex_en: My little sister is scared of dark places.
points.notes: Turns feeling adjectives (怖い, 寂しい, ほしい) into verbs describing how others seem to feel. The object of the feeling takes を.

points.meaning: might; may; possibly
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + かもしれない
points.ex_ja: 午後から雨が降るかもしれません。
points.ex_en: It might rain in the afternoon.
points.notes: About 50% certainty or less. In casual speech it is often shortened to かも.

points.meaning: probably; I suppose (plain form of でしょう)
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + だろう
points.ex_ja: 明日はたぶん晴れるだろう。
points.ex_en: It will probably be sunny tomorrow.
points.notes: Common in writing and in men's casual speech; でしょう is the polite form. Often used with たぶん or きっと, or as 〜だろうと思う.

points.meaning: should be; is expected to (based on reasoning)
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj + はずだ / na-Adj + な + はずだ / Noun + の + はずだ
points.ex_ja: 荷物は明日届くはずです。
points.ex_en: The package should arrive tomorrow.
points.notes: A confident expectation based on facts or logic, not a guess. It does not mean 'should' as a duty.

points.meaning: can't be; there's no way that
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj + はずがない / na-Adj + な + はずがない / Noun + の + はずがない
points.ex_ja: あんなにまじめな人がうそをつくはずがない。
points.ex_en: There's no way someone that earnest would lie.
points.notes: Strong denial based on reasoning. 〜ないはずだ ('should not be') is a milder expectation.

points.meaning: it's that ...; (explaining or asking for an explanation)
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj + んです / na-Adj + な + んです / Noun + な + んです
points.ex_ja: どうしたんですか。顔色が悪いですよ。
points.ex_en: What's the matter? You look pale.
points.notes: Adds a sense of explaining a situation or asking for the background. Casual forms are 〜んだ and 〜の. Overusing it can sound pushy.

points.meaning: whether or not
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + かどうか
points.ex_ja: 明日行けるかどうか、まだ分かりません。
points.ex_en: I don't know yet whether I can go tomorrow.
points.notes: Embeds a yes-no question in a sentence. For questions with a question word, use 〜か alone (何時に来るか).

points.meaning: embedded question (what, where, who, etc.)
points.formation: Question word + ... + Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + か
points.ex_ja: 会議が何時に始まるか、教えてください。
points.ex_en: Please tell me what time the meeting starts.
points.notes: After a noun or na-adjective, だ is dropped (誰の傘か知らない).

points.meaning: I think that
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj + と思う / na-Adj + だ + と思う / Noun + だ + と思う
points.ex_ja: この映画はきっと人気が出ると思う。
points.ex_en: I'm sure this movie will become popular.
points.notes: Japanese usually negates the quoted clause (来ないと思う) rather than 思う. For another person's opinion, use 〜と思っている.

points.meaning: say that; tell (quotation)
points.formation: 「Sentence」 + と言う / Sentence (plain) + と言う
points.ex_ja: 先生は「明日はテストがあります」と言いました。
points.ex_en: The teacher said, "There's a test tomorrow."
points.notes: Direct quotes go inside 「」; indirect quotes use plain forms. 〜と言っていた is common when passing on what someone said.

points.meaning: only; nothing but
points.formation: Noun + しか + Verb-nai
points.ex_ja: 財布に五百円しかない。
points.ex_en: I only have 500 yen in my wallet.
points.notes: Always paired with a negative verb. Compared with だけ, it stresses that the amount is small or not enough.

points.meaning: nothing but; only; all
points.formation: Noun + ばかり
points.ex_ja: 弟は肉ばかり食べて、野菜を食べない。
points.ex_en: My little brother eats nothing but meat and won't touch vegetables.
points.notes: Often implies there is too much of one thing. 〜てばかりいる (N3) and 〜たばかり ('just did') are separate points.

points.meaning: have just done
points.formation: Verb-ta + ばかり
points.ex_ja: 日本に来たばかりなので、まだ日本語がよく分かりません。
points.ex_en: I've only just come to Japan, so I don't understand Japanese well yet.
points.notes: Shows the speaker feels little time has passed, even if it was weeks ago. 〜たところ refers to only moments ago.

points.meaning: be about to; be in the middle of; have just done
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-te + いる / Verb-ta + ところだ
points.ex_ja: 今から出かけるところです。
points.ex_en: I'm just about to go out.
points.notes: Dictionary form: about to. 〜ているところ: in the middle of. 〜たところ: just finished. It pinpoints the stage of an action.

points.meaning: easy to; hard to
points.formation: Verb-stem + やすい / Verb-stem + にくい
points.ex_ja: このペンは書きやすいです。
points.ex_en: This pen is easy to write with.
points.notes: Both conjugate like i-adjectives. やすい can also mean 'tends to' (この服は汚れやすい).

points.meaning: start doing; finish doing; keep doing
points.formation: Verb-stem + 始める / Verb-stem + 終わる / Verb-stem + 続ける
points.ex_ja: 去年からギターを習い始めました。
points.ex_en: I started learning guitar last year.
points.notes: 〜終わる is used with actions that have a clear end (読む, 食べる, 書く). 〜終える is a more formal alternative.

points.meaning: suddenly start doing; burst out
points.formation: Verb-stem + 出す
points.ex_ja: 赤ちゃんが急に泣き出した。
points.ex_en: The baby suddenly burst out crying.
points.notes: Implies a sudden, often uncontrolled start. Unlike 〜始める, it is not used for planned actions or in requests.

points.meaning: not as ... as
points.formation: Noun / Verb-plain + ほど + i-Adj-ku + ない / na-Adj + ではない
points.ex_ja: 今年の夏は去年ほど暑くない。
points.ex_en: This summer isn't as hot as last year.
points.notes: The item before ほど is the standard of comparison. Always followed by a negative.

points.meaning: not easily; just won't; not readily
points.formation: なかなか + Verb-nai
points.ex_ja: バスがなかなか来ない。
points.ex_en: The bus just isn't coming.
points.notes: Shows that something doesn't happen as quickly or easily as hoped. With a positive form, なかなか means 'quite' (なかなかおいしい).

points.meaning: each; at a time; little by little
points.formation: Noun (quantity) + ずつ
points.ex_ja: りんごを一人に二つずつ配った。
points.ex_en: I handed out two apples to each person.

points.meaning: as many as; as much as; (with a negative) not even one
points.formation: Noun (number + counter) + も
points.ex_ja: 昨日は十時間も寝てしまった。
points.ex_en: I slept for a whole ten hours yesterday.
points.notes: Shows the speaker feels the amount is large. With 一 + counter and a negative verb, it means 'not even one'.

points.meaning: by (a deadline); before
points.formation: Noun / Verb-dict + までに
points.ex_ja: レポートは金曜日までに出してください。
points.ex_en: Please hand in the report by Friday.
points.notes: までに marks a deadline for a one-time action; まで marks how long something continues (六時まで働く).

points.meaning: sometimes; there are times when
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ことがある
points.ex_ja: 忙しいときは、朝ご飯を食べないことがあります。
points.ex_en: When I'm busy, I sometimes skip breakfast.
points.notes: Takes the dictionary or ない form. With the past form (〜たことがある) it means 'have done before' instead.

points.meaning: have to; must (conversational)
points.formation: Verb-nai + といけない / Verb-nai stem + なくちゃ
points.ex_ja: 明日は早いから、もう寝ないといけない。
points.ex_en: I have an early start tomorrow, so I need to go to bed now.
points.notes: Everyday alternatives to なければならない. なくちゃ comes from なくては; なきゃ (from なければ) is also very common.

points.meaning: please let me (do)
points.formation: Verb-nai stem + せてください (Group 1) / Verb-nai stem + させてください (Group 2)
points.ex_ja: 少し考えさせてください。
points.ex_en: Please let me think about it for a bit.
points.notes: Built on the causative て-form (する → させて). 〜させていただけませんか is more polite.

points.meaning: honorific verbs; respectful language for others' actions
points.formation: いらっしゃる（行く・来る・いる） / 召し上がる（食べる・飲む） / おっしゃる（言う） / なさる（する） / ご覧になる（見る） / くださる（くれる）
points.ex_ja: 社長は何時ごろいらっしゃいますか。
points.ex_en: Around what time will the company president be here?
points.notes: Raises the actions of people you respect, such as customers, teachers and superiors. Never use it for your own actions.

points.meaning: humble verbs; modest language for one's own actions
points.formation: 参る（行く・来る） / おる（いる） / いただく（食べる・飲む・もらう） / 申す（言う） / いたす（する） / 拝見する（見る） / 伺う（聞く・訪ねる）
points.ex_ja: 明日の午後、そちらに伺います。
points.ex_en: I'll come to your office tomorrow afternoon.
points.notes: Lowers your own actions, or your group's, toward someone you respect. 参る, おる, 申す and いたす also make speech sound formal in general.

points.meaning: (honorific) someone respected does
points.formation: お + Verb-stem + になる
points.ex_ja: 先生はもうお帰りになりました。
points.ex_en: The teacher has already gone home.
points.notes: Not used with one-syllable stems (見る, 寝る) or verbs that have special forms (行く → いらっしゃる). する-nouns take ご + Noun + になる (ご利用になる).

points.meaning: (humble) I do (for someone respected)
points.formation: お + Verb-stem + する / ご + Noun + する
points.ex_ja: 重そうですね。お持ちしましょうか。
points.ex_en: That looks heavy. Shall I carry it for you?
points.notes: Only for actions that affect or benefit the other person. お〜いたします is even more formal.

points.meaning: is; am; are (very polite copula)
points.formation: Noun / na-Adj + でございます
points.ex_ja: お手洗いはあちらでございます。
points.ex_en: The restroom is over there.
points.notes: The very polite version of です, typical of shop and hotel staff speaking to customers. ございます on its own is the polite form of あります.

points.meaning: don't mind if; it's fine if
points.formation: Verb-te + も構わない / i-Adj-ku + ても構わない / na-Adj + でも構わない / Noun + でも構わない
points.ex_ja: ここに荷物を置いても構いませんか。
points.ex_en: Do you mind if I leave my bags here?
points.notes: A little more formal than 〜てもいい. 〜なくても構わない means 'it's fine not to'.

points.meaning: the act of doing (turns a verb phrase into a noun)
points.formation: Verb-plain + の / Verb-plain + こと
points.ex_ja: 私は写真を撮るのが好きです。
points.ex_en: I like taking photos.
points.notes: の is preferred with perception verbs (見る, 聞こえる) and in casual speech; こと is needed before です/だ and in set patterns such as 〜ことができる.

points.meaning: should have (done); I wish I had
points.formation: Verb-ba + よかった / Verb-nai stem + なければよかった
points.ex_ja: もっと早く家を出ればよかった。
points.ex_en: I should have left home earlier.
points.notes: Expresses regret about the past. 〜たらよかった is a common conversational alternative.

points.meaning: why don't you ...?; how about ...?
points.formation: Verb-ta + らどう
points.ex_ja: 疲れているなら、少し休んだらどう？
points.ex_en: If you're tired, why not rest a bit?
points.notes: Often shortened to 〜たら？. Can sound pushy toward superiors; 〜たらいかがですか is the polite version.

points.meaning: had better; should
points.formation: Verb-ta / Verb-nai + ほうがいい
points.ex_ja: 熱があるなら、病院に行ったほうがいいですよ。
points.ex_en: If you have a fever, you'd better go to the hospital.
points.notes: For advice, the past form (行ったほうがいい) is the usual choice and sounds stronger. The negative uses the ない form, not the past.

points.meaning: things like A and B; A, B and so on (casual)
points.formation: Noun + とか + Noun + とか / Verb-dict + とか + Verb-dict + とか
points.ex_ja: 冷蔵庫に卵とか牛乳とかが入っています。
points.ex_en: There are things like eggs and milk in the fridge.
points.notes: More casual than 〜や〜など, and it can also list verbs or whole phrases.

points.meaning: etc.; and so on; such as
points.formation: Noun + など
points.ex_ja: 机の上に本やノートなどがあります。
points.ex_en: On the desk there are books, notebooks and so on.
points.notes: Often paired with や (AやBなど). After a single noun it softens a suggestion.

points.meaning: or something (softening a suggestion)
points.formation: Noun + でも
points.ex_ja: ちょっと休んで、コーヒーでも飲みませんか。
points.ex_en: Why don't we take a break and have a coffee or something?
points.notes: Offers one example while leaving other options open, which makes invitations and advice sound less pushy.

points.meaning: -ness (turns an adjective into a noun of degree)
points.formation: i-Adj stem + さ / na-Adj + さ
points.ex_ja: この橋の長さはどのくらいですか。
points.ex_en: How long is this bridge?
points.notes: いい becomes よさ. Common for measurements (高さ, 重さ, 大きさ, 長さ).

points.meaning: -th (ordinal: first, second, third ...)
points.formation: Noun (number + counter) + 目
points.ex_ja: 右から三つ目の建物が図書館です。
points.ex_en: The third building from the right is the library.

points.meaning: every other; at intervals of
points.formation: Noun (number + counter) + おきに
points.ex_ja: このバスは十五分おきに来ます。
points.ex_en: This bus comes every fifteen minutes.
points.notes: With days (一日おき) it skips one unit, meaning 'every other day'. With minutes or distances it usually just means 'every X'.

points.meaning: make (something) ...; change something to a state
points.formation: i-Adj-ku + する / na-Adj + に + する / Noun + に + する
points.ex_ja: テレビの音を小さくしてください。
points.ex_en: Please turn the TV down.
points.notes: Someone deliberately changes something. Compare 〜くなる / 〜になる, where the change happens by itself.

points.meaning: (a smell, sound, taste or feeling) is perceived
points.formation: Noun + がする
points.ex_ja: 台所からいいにおいがする。
points.ex_en: There's a nice smell coming from the kitchen.
points.notes: Used with におい, 音, 声, 味 and 気 (〜気がする: 'have a feeling that').

points.meaning: I wonder
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + かな / かしら
points.ex_ja: 明日は晴れるかな。
points.ex_en: I wonder if it'll be sunny tomorrow.
points.notes: A soft question, often said to oneself. かしら sounds feminine and a little old-fashioned. 〜ないかな can express a wish (早く来ないかな).

points.pattern: 〜てくれませんか / 〜ていただけませんか
points.romaji: te kuremasen ka / te itadakemasen ka
points.meaning: could you please ...? (polite request)
points.formation: Verb-te + くれませんか / Verb-te + いただけませんか
points.ex_ja: すみません、写真を撮ってくれませんか。
points.ex_en: Excuse me, could you take my picture?
points.notes: Softer than 〜てください. Politeness rises from 〜てくれませんか to 〜てもらえませんか to 〜ていただけませんか.

points.meaning: without doing; instead of doing
points.formation: Verb-nai + で
points.ex_ja: 今朝は朝ご飯を食べないで学校に行った。
points.ex_en: This morning I went to school without eating breakfast.
points.notes: 〜ずに (N3) means the same but is more formal. Differs from 〜なくて, which gives a reason.

points.meaning: no wonder; that's why; it follows that
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + という + わけだ
points.ex_ja: 三年も中国に住んでいたんですか。だから中国語が上手なわけですね。
points.ex_en: You lived in China for three years? That's why your Chinese is so good.
points.notes: States a conclusion that follows naturally from known facts, often with a feeling of 'now I understand'. Often preceded by だから, それで or どうりで.

points.meaning: it doesn't mean that; it's not that; not necessarily
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + という + わけではない
points.ex_ja: 料理が嫌いなわけではないが、毎日作る時間がない。
points.ex_en: It's not that I dislike cooking, but I don't have time to cook every day.
points.notes: A partial or soft denial of what the listener might assume. Often with いつも, 全部 or 必ずしも. Not the same as 〜わけがない, which flatly rules something out.

points.meaning: there's no way that; cannot possibly
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + わけがない
points.ex_ja: こんなに練習したんだから、負けるわけがない。
points.ex_en: We've practiced this hard, so there's no way we'll lose.
points.notes: The speaker's strong conviction that something is impossible. Casual: 〜わけない. Close to 〜はずがない, but sounds more emotional and less based on reasoning.

points.meaning: can't afford to; can't very well; must not (for social or moral reasons)
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + わけにはいかない
points.ex_ja: 明日は大事な会議があるから、休むわけにはいかない。
points.ex_en: There's an important meeting tomorrow, so I can't afford to take the day off.
points.notes: The action is physically possible but ruled out by duty, circumstances or common sense. 〜ないわけにはいかない means 'have to; can't avoid doing'.

points.meaning: it's natural that; one should; used to (nostalgia); how ...! (deep feeling)
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-ta / i-Adj / na-Adj + な + ものだ
points.ex_ja: 子どものころは、この川でよく泳いだものだ。
points.ex_en: When I was a child, I used to swim in this river a lot.
points.notes: Main uses: general truth or natural tendency, a social norm (should), a nostalgic past habit with 〜たものだ, and deep feeling (時間がたつのは早いものだ). Casual: 〜もんだ.

points.meaning: one shouldn't; it's not right to
points.formation: Verb-dict + ものではない
points.ex_ja: 人の失敗を笑うものではない。
points.ex_en: You shouldn't laugh at other people's mistakes.
points.notes: Advice based on common sense or social norms, often from an older person. Casual: 〜もんじゃない. Sounds more like general wisdom than 〜べきではない.

points.meaning: because (casual excuse or self-justification)
points.formation: Sentence + もの / もん
points.ex_ja: 「どうして食べないの？」「だって、ピーマン嫌いなんだもん。」
points.ex_en: 'Why aren't you eating?' 'Because I hate green peppers!'
points.notes: Sounds pouty or self-justifying; often begins with だって. もん is more colloquial. Used by children and among close friends; avoid at work.

points.meaning: because; since (explaining or excusing a situation)
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + な + ものだから / もので
points.ex_ja: 道がすごく混んでいたものだから、約束の時間に間に合わなかった。
points.ex_en: The roads were really crowded, so I couldn't make it on time.
points.notes: Explains or excuses something that wasn't fully under the speaker's control. The main clause can't be a command or request. もので is common in polite apologies.

points.meaning: should; the best thing is to (advice)
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ことだ
points.ex_ja: 日本語が上手になりたいなら、毎日少しずつでも話すことだ。
points.ex_en: If you want to get good at Japanese, you should speak it every day, even just a little.
points.notes: Personal advice from someone in a position to give it (teacher, parent, senior). Not used toward superiors. Compare 〜ものだ, which appeals to general norms.

points.meaning: there's no need to; don't have to
points.formation: Verb-dict + ことはない
points.ex_ja: 簡単な手術ですから、そんなに心配することはありませんよ。
points.ex_en: It's a simple operation, so there's no need to worry so much.
points.notes: Reassures or advises that something is unnecessary. Don't confuse with 〜たことはない ('have never done').

points.meaning: make it a rule to; make a point of
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ことにしている
points.ex_ja: 健康のために、週に三回はジムに通うことにしている。
points.ex_en: For my health, I make it a rule to go to the gym at least three times a week.
points.notes: A personal rule the speaker (or subject) decided on and keeps. Compare 〜ことになっている, a rule or plan set by others.

points.meaning: it has been arranged that; it's the rule that; be supposed to
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ことになっている
points.ex_ja: この寮では、夜十一時までに戻ることになっている。
points.ex_en: In this dorm, you're supposed to be back by 11 p.m.
points.notes: Rules, customs or plans decided by others (a company, school, society), not a personal choice. Compare 〜ことにしている.

points.meaning: must; do (written rule or instruction)
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + こと
points.ex_ja: レポートは、来週の金曜日までに提出すること。
points.ex_en: Reports must be submitted by next Friday.
points.notes: Ends a sentence with こと to state a rule. Found in notices, regulations and teacher-to-student instructions. Impersonal; not used toward superiors.

points.romaji: you ni iu / you ni tanomu
points.meaning: tell someone to do; ask someone to do (reported command or request)
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ように言う / ように頼む
points.ex_ja: 医者に、お酒を飲みすぎないように言われた。
points.ex_en: My doctor told me not to drink too much.
points.notes: Reports an instruction or request indirectly. Works with other verbs too: 伝える, 注意する, お願いする. Direct-quote version: 「〜てください」と言う.

points.meaning: try to; attempt to; be about to
points.formation: Verb-volitional + とする
points.ex_ja: ドアを開けようとしたが、鍵がかかっていて開かなかった。
points.ex_en: I tried to open the door, but it was locked and wouldn't open.
points.notes: Often an attempt that fails or is interrupted. 〜ようとしない = 'won't even try' (unwillingness). Compare 〜てみる, which means actually doing something to see how it goes.

points.romaji: sou ni nai / sou mo nai
points.meaning: unlikely to; doesn't look like it will
points.formation: Verb-stem + そうにない / そうもない
points.ex_ja: この雨は、夕方までやみそうにない。
points.ex_en: This rain doesn't look like it will stop before evening.
points.notes: Negative of the appearance 〜そうだ with verbs, based on what the speaker observes. More emphatic: 〜そうにもない. With adjectives use 〜なさそうだ instead.

points.meaning: keep on -ing; more and more (change in one direction)
points.formation: Verb-dict + 一方だ
points.ex_ja: この町の人口は、減る一方だ。
points.ex_en: This town's population just keeps on shrinking.
points.notes: Steady change in one direction, usually (not always) for the worse. Used with verbs of change such as 増える, 減る, 上がる, 悪くなる.

points.meaning: while; on the other hand; at the same time
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + である + 一方で
points.ex_ja: インターネットは便利な一方で、危険な面もある。
points.ex_en: The internet is convenient, but on the other hand it has its dangers.
points.notes: Presents two sides of one thing, or two parallel activities. Compare 〜に対して, which contrasts two different subjects.

points.meaning: toward; against; in contrast to
points.formation: Noun + に対して / Noun + に対する + Noun / Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な + のに対して
points.ex_ja: お客様に対して、そんな言い方をしてはいけない。
points.ex_en: You mustn't speak like that to a customer.
points.notes: Marks the target of an action, attitude or feeling, or contrasts two things. Compare 〜について, which marks the topic being discussed rather than a target.

points.meaning: about; concerning; regarding
points.formation: Noun + について / Noun + についての + Noun
points.ex_ja: 今日の授業では、日本の食文化について話し合いました。
points.ex_en: In today's class, we discussed Japanese food culture.
points.notes: Marks the topic of speaking, thinking or research. More formal: 〜に関して. Compare 〜に対して (the target of an attitude or action).

points.meaning: by (agent); by means of; due to; depending on
points.formation: Noun + によって / Noun + による + Noun
points.ex_ja: この橋は、有名な建築家によって設計された。
points.ex_en: This bridge was designed by a famous architect.
points.notes: Uses: agent of a passive (formal, for creating or discovering), cause, means, and 'varies by'. 〜によっては = 'in some cases, depending on'.

points.meaning: according to
points.formation: Noun + によると / Noun + によれば
points.ex_ja: 天気予報によると、週末は大雪になるそうだ。
points.ex_en: According to the weather forecast, there's going to be heavy snow this weekend.
points.notes: Names the source of information. The sentence usually ends in a hearsay expression such as 〜そうだ, 〜らしい or 〜ということだ.

points.meaning: not only ... but also
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + ばかりでなく
points.ex_ja: この映画は子どもばかりでなく、大人も楽しめる。
points.ex_en: Not only children but adults too can enjoy this film.
points.notes: Same meaning as 〜だけでなく but a little more formal. The second part usually contains も or まで.

points.meaning: not only ... but also
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + だけでなく
points.ex_ja: この店は料理がおいしいだけでなく、値段も安い。
points.ex_en: This restaurant not only has delicious food, it's cheap too.
points.notes: Common in both speech and writing. Casual: 〜だけじゃなくて. Slightly less formal than 〜ばかりでなく.

points.meaning: both ... and ...; not only ... but also
points.formation: Noun + も + Verb-ba + Noun + も / Noun + も + i-Adj stem + ければ + Noun + も
points.ex_ja: 彼女は歌も歌えば、ピアノも弾く。
points.ex_en: She both sings and plays the piano.
points.notes: Lists two facts of the same kind for emphasis; contrasting pairs (いいときも悪いときも) are very common. Compare 〜し, which lists reasons.

points.meaning: typical of; befitting; truly like
points.formation: Noun + らしい
points.ex_ja: 今日は春らしい暖かい一日だった。
points.ex_en: Today was a warm, truly spring-like day.
points.notes: Having the qualities you expect of the noun. Negative: 〜らしくない ('not like'). Differs from the hearsay 〜らしい (N4) and from 〜っぽい (looks like X but isn't).

points.meaning: -ish; -like; tends to (casual)
points.formation: Noun / Verb-stem / i-Adj stem + っぽい
points.ex_ja: この服はちょっと子どもっぽいから、別のにしよう。
points.ex_en: This outfit is a bit childish, so let's go with a different one.
points.notes: Noun + っぽい: seems like X though it isn't (大人っぽい). Verb-stem + っぽい: tends to (怒りっぽい). Compare 〜らしい, which means truly typical of X.

points.meaning: -ic; -al; in terms of
points.formation: Noun + 的な + Noun / Noun + 的に
points.ex_ja: 日本の伝統的な料理を食べてみたい。
points.ex_en: I'd like to try traditional Japanese food.
points.notes: Turns a (usually kanji) noun into a na-adjective: 的な before nouns, 的に before verbs and adjectives. Many are best learned as words: 具体的, 基本的, 積極的.

points.meaning: like; as; such as
points.formation: Verb-plain / Noun + の + ような / ように
points.ex_ja: 私も、あなたのような優しい看護師になりたいです。
points.ex_en: I want to become a kind nurse like you, too.
points.notes: ような comes before nouns, ように before verbs and adjectives. AのようなB can also mean 'B such as A'. Casual: 〜みたいな / 〜みたいに.

points.meaning: just like; as if
points.formation: まるで + Verb-plain / Noun + の + ようだ
points.ex_ja: この部屋は広くて明るくて、まるでホテルのようだ。
points.ex_en: This room is so big and bright, it's just like a hotel.
points.notes: まるで signals a figurative comparison: it only seems so. Casual: まるで〜みたいだ. Compare N2 〜かのようだ.

points.meaning: must be; surely; no doubt
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + に違いない
points.ex_ja: 隣の家は何日も電気が消えている。家族で旅行に出かけたに違いない。
points.ex_en: The lights next door have been off for days. The family must have gone on a trip.
points.notes: Strong conviction based on evidence or intuition; a slightly written tone. Compare 〜に決まっている, which is more subjective and conversational.

points.meaning: certainly; is bound to; of course
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + に決まっている
points.ex_ja: 練習もしないで試合に出たら、負けるに決まっている。
points.ex_en: If you play the match without practicing, you're bound to lose.
points.notes: A very confident, subjective judgment, common in conversation (〜に決まってる). More assertive than 〜に違いない and not suited to formal writing.

points.meaning: have a feeling that; feel like
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な + 気がする / Verb-plain / Noun + の + ような + 気がする
points.ex_ja: この人とは、どこかで会ったことがある気がする。
points.ex_en: I feel like I've met this person somewhere before.
points.notes: A vague, intuitive impression rather than a firm judgment; ような気がする is even softer. Different from N4 〜がする (a smell, sound or taste).

points.meaning: without doing
points.formation: Verb-nai stem + ずに
points.ex_ja: けさは朝ご飯を食べずに家を出た。
points.ex_en: This morning I left home without eating breakfast.
points.notes: More formal, written-style equivalent of 〜ないで. Irregular: する → せずに (not しずに), 来る → 来ずに (こずに).

points.meaning: as it is; unchanged; while still (in a state)
points.formation: Verb-ta / Verb-nai / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + まま
points.ex_ja: エアコンをつけたまま寝てしまい、風邪をひいた。
points.ex_en: I fell asleep with the air conditioner on and caught a cold.
points.notes: An expected change hasn't happened and the state continues. Often suggests something unusual or undesirable (leaving the lights on, shoes on indoors).

points.meaning: while (before it changes); before it's too late; in the course of
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-te + いる / Verb-nai / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + うちに
points.ex_ja: 若いうちに、いろいろな国を旅行したほうがいい。
points.ex_en: You should travel to lots of countries while you're young.
points.notes: Do something while a condition lasts, before it changes; or a change that happens unnoticed during an activity. Compare 〜間に, which marks a fixed period without that urgency.

points.pattern: 〜ところに / 〜ところへ / 〜ところを
points.romaji: tokoro ni / tokoro e / tokoro o
points.meaning: just when; at the moment (someone arrives or something interrupts)
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-te + いる / Verb-ta + ところに / ところへ / ところを
points.ex_ja: 出かけようとしているところに、友達から電話がかかってきた。
points.ex_en: Just as I was about to go out, a friend called.
points.notes: ところに/へ: something happens or someone arrives at that moment, often interrupting. ところを: the scene is the object of a verb like 見る, 見つかる, 助ける. Set phrase: お忙しいところを.

points.meaning: the more ... the more
points.formation: Verb-ba + Verb-dict + ほど / i-Adj stem + ければ + i-Adj + ほど / na-Adj + なら + na-Adj + な + ほど
points.ex_ja: 日本語は、勉強すればするほど面白くなる。
points.ex_en: The more you study Japanese, the more interesting it gets.
points.notes: The same word is repeated, first in the ば/なら form, then in plain form. The first part can be dropped: 考えるほど分からなくなる.

points.meaning: to the extent that; so ... that
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + ほど
points.ex_ja: 昨日は、立っていられないほど疲れていた。
points.ex_en: Yesterday I was so tired I could hardly stand.
points.notes: Shows degree with an example or comparison. Often interchangeable with 〜くらい, but ほど sounds more formal and suits high degrees; it can't mark something as minimal.

points.meaning: to the extent that; so ... that; at least (something minimal)
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + くらい
points.ex_ja: おなかが痛くて、歩けないくらいだった。
points.ex_en: My stomach hurt so much I could barely walk.
points.notes: Like 〜ほど, shows degree. くらい can also mark something as small or easy ('at least; such a simple thing as'), a use ほど doesn't have.

points.meaning: even
points.formation: Noun + さえ / Noun + でさえ / Noun + にさえ
points.ex_ja: 忙しくて、昼ご飯を食べる時間さえなかった。
points.ex_en: I was so busy I didn't even have time to eat lunch.
points.notes: Gives an extreme example, implying 'so naturally the others too'. More formal than 〜も or 〜でも in this sense. As a subject: 〜でさえ. Compare N1 〜すら.

points.meaning: if only; as long as; provided that
points.formation: Noun + さえ + Verb-ba / Verb-stem + さえ + すれば / Verb-te + さえ + いれば
points.ex_ja: このアプリさえあれば、どこでも日本語の勉強ができる。
points.ex_en: As long as you have this app, you can study Japanese anywhere.
points.notes: Stresses that this one condition is enough by itself, or is the only thing missing.

points.meaning: precisely; it is ... that; (strong emphasis)
points.formation: Noun + こそ
points.ex_ja: 「いつもありがとう。」「いえ、こちらこそ。」
points.ex_en: 'Thanks for everything.' 'No, thank you!'
points.notes: Singles out one thing as the very one that matters. こちらこそ is a set reply: 'the thanks/pleasure is mine'. Related N2 forms: 〜からこそ, 〜てこそ.

points.meaning: as; in the role or capacity of
points.formation: Noun + として / Noun + としての + Noun
points.ex_ja: 兄は、エンジニアとしてアメリカの会社で働いている。
points.ex_en: My older brother works as an engineer at an American company.
points.notes: States a role, status or category. Compare 〜にとって, which states from whose point of view a judgment is made.

points.meaning: for; to (from the standpoint of)
points.formation: Noun + にとって / Noun + にとっての + Noun
points.ex_ja: 私にとって、家族は何よりも大切なものです。
points.ex_en: To me, family is more important than anything.
points.notes: Followed by an evaluation (大切だ, 難しい, 便利だ). Not for actions or attitudes toward someone; use 〜に対して for those.

points.meaning: for (considering it's); unexpectedly for
points.formation: Verb-plain / Noun + にしては
points.ex_ja: 初めて作ったにしては、このケーキはよくできている。
points.ex_en: For a first attempt, this cake turned out really well.
points.notes: The result is different from what you'd expect of X. Doesn't follow adjectives; compare 〜わりに, which can and focuses on degree (price, age, effort).

points.meaning: even if; even considering; granted that
points.formation: Verb-plain / Noun + にしても
points.ex_ja: 忙しかったにしても、電話一本ぐらいできたでしょう。
points.ex_en: Even if you were busy, you could at least have made one phone call.
points.notes: Accepts a point, then says it doesn't change the speaker's view. Often accepts a fact; compare 〜としても, which is more purely hypothetical.

points.meaning: regarding; concerning; related to
points.formation: Noun + に関して / Noun + に関する + Noun
points.ex_ja: 新しいサービスに関してご質問がある方は、受付までどうぞ。
points.ex_en: Anyone with questions regarding the new service, please come to the reception desk.
points.notes: More formal than 〜について; common in business, news and writing. Before a noun, use に関する (or に関しての).

points.meaning: compared to; in comparison with
points.formation: Noun + に比べて / Verb-dict + のに比べて
points.ex_ja: 今年の夏は、去年に比べてずいぶん涼しい。
points.ex_en: This summer is much cooler compared to last year.
points.notes: Also 〜と比べて, 〜に比べると and 〜に比べれば. Sets two things side by side more explicitly than 〜より.

points.meaning: instead of; on behalf of; replacing
points.formation: Noun + に代わって / Noun + に代わり
points.ex_ja: 入院中の社長に代わって、副社長があいさつをした。
points.ex_en: The vice president gave the speech on behalf of the president, who is in hospital.
points.notes: Someone acts for another person, or something new replaces something old. Written form: 〜に代わり. Compare 〜代わりに (instead of doing; in exchange for).

points.meaning: instead of; in exchange for; to make up for
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + 代わりに
points.ex_ja: 今日は外で食べる代わりに、家でカレーを作った。
points.ex_en: Instead of eating out today, I made curry at home.
points.notes: Three uses: substitution (instead of), exchange (in return for), and compensation (a downside balanced by an upside).

points.meaning: in accordance with; following; as ... (so ...)
points.formation: Noun + に従って / Verb-dict + に従って
points.ex_ja: 係の人の指示に従って、落ち着いて避難してください。
points.ex_en: Please evacuate calmly, following the staff's instructions.
points.notes: With nouns such as rules or instructions: 'following, obeying'. With Verb-dict: proportional change like 〜につれて, in a more formal tone.

points.meaning: as (one thing changes, another changes too)
points.formation: Verb-dict / Noun + につれて
points.ex_ja: 年をとるにつれて、朝早く目が覚めるようになった。
points.ex_en: As I've gotten older, I've started waking up early in the morning.
points.notes: Both halves describe gradual change. The main clause can't be a request or the speaker's intention. Close to 〜に従って and 〜とともに.

points.meaning: together with; along with; as; at the same time as
points.formation: Noun + とともに / Verb-dict + とともに
points.ex_ja: 社長は、社員とともに新しい工場の完成を喜んだ。
points.ex_en: The company president celebrated the completion of the new factory together with the staff.
points.notes: Formal version of 〜と一緒に. Also marks events happening at the same moment, or proportional change like 〜につれて.

points.meaning: every time; whenever
points.formation: Verb-dict / Noun + の + たびに
points.ex_ja: この写真を見るたびに、大学時代を思い出す。
points.ex_en: Every time I look at this photo, I remember my university days.
points.notes: Each time A happens, B happens too. More emphatic than 〜と or 〜ときはいつも.

points.meaning: every; each; at intervals of
points.formation: Noun + ごとに / Verb-dict + ごとに
points.ex_ja: このバスは十五分ごとに出ています。
points.ex_en: This bus leaves every fifteen minutes.
points.notes: Regular repetition, or each unit in turn. With Verb-dict it's close to 〜たびに. Careful: 一日ごとに = every day, but 一日おきに (N4) = every other day.

points.meaning: right in the middle of; while (busy with)
points.formation: Verb-te + いる / Noun + の + 最中に
points.ex_ja: 大事な会議の最中に、携帯電話が鳴ってしまった。
points.ex_en: My cell phone went off right in the middle of an important meeting.
points.notes: Stresses the height of an activity, usually when something unexpected interrupts it. Stronger than 〜中に or 〜ている間に. Also 〜最中だ.

points.meaning: while (at it); on the occasion of; since one is doing it anyway
points.formation: Verb-dict / Verb-ta / Noun + の + ついでに
points.ex_ja: 郵便局へ行くついでに、この手紙も出してきてくれる？
points.ex_en: Since you're going to the post office, could you mail this letter too?
points.notes: The main action happens anyway; the second is added because it's convenient. Compare N1 〜がてら.

points.meaning: thanks to; because of (good result)
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + おかげで
points.ex_ja: 先輩が手伝ってくれたおかげで、仕事が早く終わった。
points.ex_en: Thanks to my senior colleague's help, the work was finished early.
points.notes: Cause of a good result, with a feeling of gratitude. Sometimes used sarcastically for a bad result (君のおかげで遅刻したよ). Compare 〜せいで (blame).

points.meaning: because of; due to (bad result, blame)
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + せいで
points.ex_ja: 電車が遅れたせいで、面接に遅刻してしまった。
points.ex_en: Because the train was delayed, I was late for my interview.
points.notes: Cause of a bad result, placing blame. 〜のせいにする = 'blame something on'. The opposite feeling of 〜おかげで.

points.meaning: the moment; just as (something unexpected happens)
points.formation: Verb-ta + とたん / とたんに
points.ex_ja: 立ち上がったとたんに、めまいがした。
points.ex_en: The moment I stood up, I felt dizzy.
points.notes: The second event is sudden and outside the speaker's control. Not used for the speaker's own planned actions, requests or intentions.

points.meaning: when I did A, (I found that) B; upon doing, I discovered
points.formation: Verb-ta + ら ... Verb-ta
points.ex_ja: 窓を開けたら、外は一面の雪だった。
points.ex_en: When I opened the window, everything outside was covered in snow.
points.notes: After an action, the speaker notices or discovers something. The second clause is past and outside the speaker's control. 〜と〜た is a more written equivalent.

points.meaning: even if; no matter (casual)
points.formation: Verb-ta + って / i-Adj-ku + たって / na-Adj / Noun + だって
points.ex_ja: 今から急いだって、もう間に合わないよ。
points.ex_en: Even if you hurry now, you won't make it.
points.notes: Colloquial form of 〜ても / 〜でも, often with いくら or question words. だって also means 'because' at the start of a sentence, and 'even' after nouns.

points.meaning: it's not that ... not; can if necessary; not impossible
points.formation: Verb-nai / i-Adj-ku + ない / na-Adj + でない + ことはない
points.ex_ja: 辛い料理は食べられないことはないけど、あまり好きじゃない。
points.ex_en: It's not that I can't eat spicy food, but I don't really like it.
points.notes: A double negative giving a hesitant 'yes'. Also 〜ないこともない. Don't confuse with Verb-dict + ことはない ('there's no need to').

points.pattern: 〜てしょうがない / 〜てしかたがない
points.romaji: te shou ga nai / te shikata ga nai
points.meaning: extremely; can't help (feeling); unbearably
points.formation: Verb-te / i-Adj-ku + て / na-Adj + で + しょうがない / しかたがない
points.ex_ja: 昨日あまり寝ていないので、眠くてしょうがない。
points.ex_en: I barely slept last night, so I'm terribly sleepy.
points.notes: For feelings and sensations the speaker can't control. しょうがない is more casual. Unlike 〜てたまらない, it also works with spontaneous verbs like 気になる or 涙が出る.

points.meaning: unbearably; dying to; extremely (feeling)
points.formation: Verb-te / i-Adj-ku + て / na-Adj + で + たまらない
points.ex_ja: この部屋はエアコンがなくて、暑くてたまらない。
points.ex_en: This room has no air conditioning; it's unbearably hot.
points.notes: Strong, direct feelings or bodily sensations; very common with desire (〜たくてたまらない). Not used for objective facts. Compare 〜てしかたがない.

points.meaning: only after; not until
points.formation: Verb-te + はじめて
points.ex_ja: 病気になってはじめて、健康のありがたさが分かった。
points.ex_en: It was only after I got sick that I appreciated how precious good health is.
points.notes: Something is realized or becomes possible only after an experience; often followed by 分かる, 気づく or 知る. Also written 〜て初めて.

points.meaning: do nothing but; keep on doing (critical)
points.formation: Verb-te + ばかりいる
points.ex_ja: 弟は休みの日、ゲームをしてばかりいる。
points.ex_en: On his days off, my younger brother does nothing but play games.
points.notes: A repeated or constant action, usually with criticism or dissatisfaction. Compare N4 Noun + ばかり (甘い物ばかり食べる).

points.meaning: should; all you need to do is; I hope (with のに/けど: I wish)
points.formation: Verb-ba + いい / i-Adj stem + ければ + いい
points.ex_ja: 「この書類、どこに出せばいいですか。」「二階の受付に出してください。」
points.ex_en: 'Where should I hand in this form?' 'Please take it to the reception desk on the second floor.'
points.notes: Asks for or gives advice (〜ばいいですか = 'what should I do?'). 〜ばいいのに = 'I wish'. 〜たらいい is a near-synonym; 〜ほうがいい sounds more insistent.

points.meaning: in the case of; if; in the event that
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + 場合（は）
points.ex_ja: 雨の場合は、試合は中止になります。
points.ex_en: In case of rain, the game will be canceled.
points.notes: Typical of instructions, rules and announcements about possible situations. Unlike 〜たら, it is not used to narrate a one-off past event.

points.meaning: if; supposing that; assuming
points.formation: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + だ / Noun + だ + とすれば / としたら
